IDE override remains intentionally explicit. Normalizer cannot launder a failed build through stale output.

limitations: These are actual shell executions using synthetic wrapper/framework fixtures, not new Xcode execution by this reviewer. No diagnosis of historical launch crashes is established.

limitations: The current evidence is macOS-hosted with a GNU-shaped shim, not an actual Linux job result. Portable Python metadata semantics are source-backed.

findings.root_cause_and_correction: Validation-only JDK21 helper authenticates every non-signature-metadata JAR payload by reading verified entries to EOF, checks every signer against the approved SHA256, validates an approved self-signed leaf as a non-anchor PKIX certificate with code-signing AlgorithmChecker, and only then creates public-only CREATE_NEW temporary trust. Strict jarsigner remains mandatory. Timestamp trust is separately validated against original JDK public roots before timestamp affects leaf validity.
counter_evidence: No blanket exit4 waiver; approved fingerprint, integrity, unsigned-payload, weak-algorithm, validity and code-purpose controls stay enforced. Ordinary META-INF payload is not treated as signature metadata.
JDK21 trusted-leaf short circuit was checked against retained exact-tag source; helper compensates before adding the leaf as temporary trust.
TSA validation is isolated from upload trust; non-self-signed untrusted CA does not become trusted. No Store keys accessed.
Runtime Java feature guard and narrow internal API exports fail closed; helper does not ship in application artifacts.
findings.regression: Twenty real disposable synthetic certificate/JAR policy tests plus one owned TERM-resistant descendant-cleanup test pass. Actual signed payload tampering, unsigned payload, wrong/additional signer, invalid/weak certificate and timestamp trust boundary negatives execute.
limitations: No Store-signed AAB or private credential used. Positive full RFC3161 integration and wider algorithm matrix remain unexecuted.
The helper adds bounds but is not a full hostile-ZIP sandbox; existing unzip -tqq precedes helper bounds. No broader archive-security claim.
findings.compatibility: No blanket exit4 waiver, no weak-algorithm/fingerprint/unsigned-payload bypass; Java helper is release tooling only.
